adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: New temporal headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, elevated inflammatory markers, and transient monocular visual loss in a patient older than 50 is the classic cranial ischemic phenotype of giant cell arteritis.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Migraine can include transient visual symptoms and temporal pain, but age >50, new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, and markedly elevated ESR/CRP establish a vasculitic syndrome. The Q0618 canonical hit is only a distractor explanation in a Behçet item, not a prior GCA main construct.
